svg.title: A client with rising intracranial pressure now has a right pupil that is dilated and does not react to the penlight. The nurse recognizes compression of which cranial nerve?
svg.desc: Pupil constriction is carried by the oculomotor nerve (CN III) ; as the brain swells and herniates it compresses CN III, leaving a fixed, dilated pupil on that side, a late sign of increased ICP. CN II carries vision, not the motor response of the pupil, so it is the tempting but wrong choice.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Neurologic Dysfunction &
Cerebrovascular Disorders
Read the situation
A client with rising intracranial pressure
now has a right pupil that is dilated and
does not react to the penlight. The nurse
recognizes compression of which cranial
nerve?
What fits here
Cranial nerve III (oculomotor)
Why it fits
Pupil constriction is carried by the
oculomotor nerve (CN III) ; as the brain
swells and herniates it compresses CN III,
leaving a fixed, dilated pupil on that
side, a late sign of increased ICP. CN II
carries vision, not the motor response of
the pupil, so it is the tempting but wrong
choice.
